name: Paneer Bhurji

ingredients.name: Paneer (cottage cheese), full-fat
ingredients.householdMeasure: a fifth of a 500 g block; about ¾ cup when crumbled

ingredients.name: Onion (pyaz/kanda)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1 small onion, finely chopped (about ⅓ cup)

ingredients.name: Tomato (tamatar)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1 small ripe tomato, finely chopped (about ⅓ cup)

ingredients.name: Ginger (adrak)
ingredients.householdMeasure: ½-inch piece, finely chopped or grated

ingredients.name: Garlic (lahsun)
ingredients.householdMeasure: 1 large or 2 small cloves, finely chopped

equipment: Plate or bowl, to crumble the paneer by hand (or a box grater)
Kadai or 8-inch non-stick or heavy pan
Measuring spoons (a normal teaspoon is fine)

steps.title: Crumble the paneer
steps.text: Break 100 g paneer into a plate and crumble it with your fingers into small, uneven bits (about pea size), or grate it on the large holes of a grater.
steps.tip: Hard fridge paneer crumbles poorly; soak the block in warm water for 10 min first, then pat dry.
steps.visualCue: Coarse, uneven crumbs, no big lumps; not a smooth paste
steps.videoShot: Fingers crumbling a paneer block onto a plate.

steps.title: Chop the onion
steps.visualCue: Small even pieces, about ⅓ cup

steps.title: Chop the tomato
steps.text: Finely chop 1 small ripe tomato (60 g).
steps.visualCue: Small red pieces with their juice, about ⅓ cup

steps.title: Chop ginger, garlic and chilli
steps.text: Finely chop ½-inch ginger (3 g), 1 large garlic clove (3 g) and ½–1 green chilli (2 g).
steps.tip: 1 tsp ready ginger-garlic paste works instead (most recipe sites use paste).
steps.visualCue: Three small heaps of fine pieces
steps.cameraCheck: The three heaps on the board

steps.title: Chop the coriander
steps.text: Chop 1 tsp (2 g) fresh coriander leaves.

steps.title: Heat the fat
steps.text: Put the kadai on medium heat with 1 tsp (5 g) oil and 1 tsp (5 g) butter.

steps.title: Temper the cumin
steps.tip: If the cumin blackens at once, the pan is too hot; lower the heat.
steps.visualCue: Seeds sizzle and turn one shade darker; nutty smell

steps.title: Cook the onion
steps.text: Add the chopped onion and stir now and then on medium heat.
steps.visualCue: Soft and translucent with light golden edges; sweet smell

steps.title: Add ginger, garlic and chilli
steps.text: Add the chopped ginger, garlic and green chilli; stir.
steps.visualCue: Raw garlic smell gone; garlic just turning pale gold
steps.videoShot: Ginger and garlic tipped onto the onions.

steps.title: Add the powders
steps.text: Lower the heat and add a large pinch of turmeric, ½ tsp Kashmiri chilli powder and ¼ tsp coriander powder. Stir.
steps.tip: Add 1 tsp water if the powders start to stick.
steps.visualCue: Onions turn orange-red; spices smell toasted, not burnt

steps.title: Add the tomato and salt
steps.text: Add the chopped tomato and ¼ tsp (1.5 g) salt; stir and turn the heat back to medium.

steps.title: Cook the tomato down
steps.text: Cook, stirring and pressing the tomato with the spoon.
steps.visualCue: Tomato soft and mushy, masala thick, a little fat shows at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: The edge of the masala showing fat

steps.title: Add the paneer
steps.text: Tip in the crumbled paneer and mix gently so every crumb is coated.
steps.visualCue: Paneer evenly orange-yellow, no white patches
steps.videoShot: Paneer crumbs folded into red masala.

steps.title: Add milk, garam masala and kasuri methi
steps.text: Sprinkle 1 tbsp (15 ml) milk, ¼ tsp garam masala, and crush ¼ tsp kasuri methi between your palms over the pan. Mix.
steps.visualCue: Bhurji looks moist, not dry; warm, sweet smell
steps.cameraCheck: The kasuri methi flecks on the bhurji
steps.videoShot: Palms rubbing kasuri methi over the pan.

steps.title: Heat through briefly
steps.text: Cook on low heat, stirring gently.
steps.tip: Do not cook longer than 2 minutes after the paneer goes in; overcooked paneer turns hard and chewy (the warning in almost every source).
steps.visualCue: Steaming, soft and moist; crumbs still distinct
steps.cameraCheck: A spoonful lifted to show soft crumbs

steps.title: Taste and adjust
steps.text: Turn off the heat, taste and add a pinch more salt only if needed.
steps.visualCue: Mildly spicy, savoury, a little tangy from tomato
steps.videoShot: A spoon of bhurji lifted for tasting.

steps.title: Garnish and serve
steps.text: Scatter the chopped coriander, add a squeeze of lemon if you like, and transfer to a plate.
steps.visualCue: Moist orange-yellow crumbs with green flecks
steps.videoShot: Coriander scattered over the bhurji, steam rising.

reasons: about 21 g protein, about 245 mg calcium and B12 from paneer, no frying, no flour and no sugar, ready in 20 minutes, and only 2 tsp fat added. Points off for about 16 g saturated fat (about three quarters of a day's limit, mostly from full-fat paneer), about 625 mg sodium and little fibre (about 2.8 g) or vegetable. Restaurant and street versions usually use more butter or oil, sometimes cream or cheese, and come with buttered pav, often making it a 700–900 kcal meal.

researchRating.basis: a very popular quick paneer dish; Indian Healthy Recipes' version shows 5 from 176 votes, Cook With Manali 5 from 18, Manjula's Kitchen 5 from 1; Veg Recipes of India's page has at least two pages of comments; it is published by almost every major Indian recipe site and chef (Hebbar's Kitchen, Ranveer Brar, Kunal Kapur, Archana's Kitchen, Saveur), is a named signature dish of Bhagat Tarachand, and is sold as a frozen ready product by Hyperpure. Points off because it is seen as a simple everyday or backup dish rather than a favourite, and Mumbai delivery menus list it far less often than egg bhurji or paneer gravies. Platform dish ratings were not used.

storage: Fridge-safe in a closed box for up to 2 days (cool within 1 hour). Freezer: not recommended; frozen crumbled paneer turns dry and grainy. Reheat in a pan on low with 1–2 tbsp milk or water, stirring gently, for 1–2 min; or microwave covered in 30-second bursts. Do not overheat or the paneer turns rubbery.
leftoverRemix: Paneer bhurji stuffed paratha or chilla. Mash the leftover bhurji a little, stuff it into whole-wheat dough and roll a paratha (cook on a tawa with ½ tsp oil), or spread it over a besan or moong dal chilla and fold it (Veg Recipes of India also uses it as a grilled sandwich filling).
burnOff: about 5.8 km of running (405 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 8.1 km of brisk walking (about 1 h 40 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With 2 phulkas (about 585 kcal): about 8.4 km running or 11.7 km walking (est.).

navratri.reason: paneer, tomato, green chilli, ginger and milk are allowed in the common vrat rule set; skip onion and garlic, use sendha namak instead of table salt, and leave out turmeric, garam masala and coriander powder if your family avoids them (cumin and black pepper are widely used).

ekadashi.reason: no grains or pulses in the dish; skip onion and garlic (common rule set; family rules on spices vary). Serve without roti or pav.

jain.reason: onion, garlic and fresh ginger are root vegetables; use the Jain variant (tomato-capsicum base with sonth).

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; quick, high-protein and not too heavy with 2 rotis for sehri or iftar; moderately salty (about 625 mg sodium), so drink water.

jain.reason: onion, garlic and fresh ginger are root vegetables; skip all three, use dry ginger powder (sonth), more tomato and capsicum (see Jain variant).

vegan.reason: paneer, butter and milk are dairy; use firm tofu and oil (see Vegan variant, Tofu Bhurji).

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, no meat, so it fits a pescatarian diet.

sattvik.reason: skip onion and garlic, keep ginger, add more tomato and capsicum (see Sattvik variant).

glutenFree.reason: no wheat, maida, rava or besan, and the main recipe uses no hing; if you add hing, use a gluten-free one, as most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour. Check the garam masala label for added flour. The dhaba gravy style thickened with besan is still gluten-free; pav, roti and paratha are not.

dairyFree.reason: paneer, butter and milk are dairy; use the Tofu Bhurji variant.
